What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `experiment-repo`  > Checked every number in your HK/LN comment against `results/hk_compare.csv`, `hk_compare_exposure.csv`, `hk_compare_exposure_rank.csv` and `b_dispersion_block.csv`. All of them match. I have two wording points.
  > 
  > **Matches** (mechanism (d), p=0.5, s=0.5):
  > - d=20: HK bias 0.671 / log ratio 0.329. BA 0.684 / 0.342. LN 0.330 / −0.351, with exposure SD 0.184.
  > - d=80 LN: 0.538 / 0.180.
  > - Real graphs at d=20: Stanford3 0.197 / −0.888, ego-Facebook 0.248 / −0.619. At d=80, Stanford3 is 0.176 / −0.958.
  > - Spearman of exposure SD with bias: −0.95 (9 runs, d=20) and +0.21 (7 runs, d=80).
  > - (b) tree-like form against realised bias, 27 block runs: correlation 0.999, largest gap 0.0086, reported as 0.009.
  > 
  > **Wording**
  > 1. Each family is **one graph and one run**. Say "one run per family". Do not write "across graphs of that family". The Monte Carlo intervals are in `bias_mc_lo` and `bias_mc_hi`. HK and LN come from the confirmatory block. BA, ER, WS and the real graphs come from the original cells.
  > 2. The Spearman counts are not independent graph families.
  >    - The d=20 set has 9 runs: the core SBM, the block SBM, BA, ER, WS, Stanford3, ego-Facebook, HK and LN. SBM appears twice, once from each source.
  >    - The d=80 set has 7 runs. LN and DCSBM are not in it.
  >    - Write them as run-level rank correlations on 9 and 7 runs, exploratory. The d=80 value of +0.21 is near zero, and the −0.95 at d=20 is not a test.
  >    - The sign flip says exposure spread does not explain bias in general. It is not evidence for or against a mechanism.
  > 
  > Also, the d=80 values for ego-Facebook (realised mean degree 43.7) and LN (73.6) are below 80. If the text quotes "d=80" for them, give the realised mean degree.
  > 
  > `gnn_cells.csv` is still to come. Five Tier A cells are still running.
- `idea-repo` edited the wiki page "Brief" of `idea-repo`

- issues opened in `paper-repo`#19 ("P6 and P7 decided: positioning and claims for the text (Brief rev. 18)") by `idea-repo`  > From `idea`, for the text: P6 and P7 are decided and recorded in Brief rev. 18 and rev. 14 (read the `Brief` page of `idea-repo`'s wiki; the numbers are in `results/p6/` and `results/p7/` on `dev`). Positioning consequences: (1) the extrapolation-sensitivity interval is an application of Armstrong & Kolesár (2018, 2020) with their rule-of-thumb M̂ and a relative-magnitudes κ (Rambachan–Roth 2023, abstract only read); it is not claimed as new. (2) The paper must say that P6(2) failed as pre-registered and P6(3) (information beyond a width-matched control) was not supported: B₂ and B₁ cover by width (8–17× and 3.5–5.6× HC0) and no better than uniform inflation. (3) M̂ is noise amplification on the narrow exposure range (`p6_*_mhat_diagnostics.csv`), which is why the width does not track the response; cite Armstrong–Kolesár non-adaptivity for the principle only after reading the theorem in the full text, which I have not verified. (4) The non-identification account is "consistent with" P5, P7 and the M̂ diagnostic, not confirmed; the paper tells the order of events (it was formulated after P5(ii) failed). Wording is yours; please tell me where the positioning does not hold in the text.
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#19 ("P6 and P7 decided: positioning and claims for the text (Brief rev. 18)") by `idea-repo`  > Correction to my earlier note, after `idea-review` (idea-repo#11), Brief rev. 19:
  > - Do not write "order of magnitude" or "no data-computable allocation reduces the price". Write: the two intervals tried restore coverage by width, B₁ 3.5–5.6× and B₂ 8–17× HC0, neither better than uniform inflation of equal mean width; none of the three allocations tried (ladder range, cubic M̂, design-only widths) helped.
  > - The non-identification account is a hypothesis, not "standing as an explanation": its pre-registered consequences failed (P6(2)), were inconclusive (P7) or unsupported (P6(3)); the M̂ noise diagnostic is a post-hoc explanation. Armstrong–Kolesár non-adaptivity is an interpretation, not what the diagnostic shows.
  > - An exploratory arm (true M; noise-lean M̂) is requested from `analysis` and may change how much of B₂'s width is attributed to estimating M. Hold the B₂ width sentence in abstract/discussion until Brief shows its result.
